summary: Independent review of the 60-row TiO2 phospho SILAC SDRF (30 raw x light/heavy). Every technical value was re-derived from primary evidence: raw-header scan events read by this reviewer for all 30 files, mqpar.xml, Experimental_Design.xlsx, PMC10713615 Methods and the PRIDE record. The override of the design sheet's MS-method column holds: the raw headers give RW8 = CID at 30 NCE with ITMS MS2, RW9 = CID with multistage activation at 35 NCE with ITMS MS2, and RW10 = HCD at 45 NCE with FTMS MS2, matching both the Methods and the sample names embedded in the files. No blocker or important finding.

reviewer_context.context: fresh subagent without producer transcript; read only the brief, the artifact, the spec and primary sources it fetched itself (PRIDE files/all and project, Europe PMC full text, FTP design sheet, mqpar.xml, raw-file range reads); prior review-* dirs not read

spec_compliance.evidence: I resolved ms-proteomics 1.1.0, vertebrates 1.1.0 and clinical-metadata 1.0.0 with spec/scripts/resolve_templates.py. Every column is licensed (characteristics[genotype] comes from clinical-metadata), no required or recommended column is missing, and every reserved word is allowed by its column's allow_* flag. vertebrates and clinical-metadata are not mutually exclusive. There are 60 rows with 41 fields each. Modification strings follow NT/AC/TA|PP/MT, and the Acetyl uses PP=Protein N-term. Collision energy follows the '{value} NCE' pattern.

ontology_integrity.evidence: I looked up 23 accessions by obo_id in OLS4. All of them are non-obsolete and their labels match exactly: UBERON:0000956, CL:0010012, MONDO:0100039, PATO:0000461, EFO:0002567, PATO:0000384, MS:1001742, MS:1001251, MS:1001309, MS:1000133, MS:1000422, MS:1000083, MS:1000484, PRIDE:0000627, NCBITaxon:10090, and UNIMOD 481/188/259/267/21/1/4/35. EFO:0010806 is a child of EFO:0009090, as TERMS requires. SILAC light and SILAC heavy are PRIDE:0000326 and PRIDE:0000325. OLS has no PSI-MS term for multistage activation, so encoding it as CID is justified. sdrf-tools check found 21 of 21 terms verified, 0 UNIMOD swaps.

source_evidence.evidence: PMC10713615 Methods state: male E16.5 embryos; Cdkl5 +/Y or -/Y; C57 Bl/6 backcross; one K8R10 (heavy) and one K4R6 (light) dish per embryo; 3x heavy WT/light KO and 3x heavy KO/light WT; trypsin, then Lys-C followed by trypsin; TiO2 enrichment; LTQ Orbitrap Velos; Top10 with CID at 30%, MSA at 35% and HCD at 45% (HCD MS2 in the Orbitrap). The raw-header scan events I read for all 30 files confirm activation type, NCE, MS2 analyzer and instrument per file, and the embedded sample names (C1-C4, E1-E6 + method) agree. mqpar.xml confirms Trypsin/P, fixed Carbamidomethyl (C), variable Oxidation (M), Acetyl (Protein N-term) and Phospho (STY), labels Arg6;Lys4 and Arg10;Lys8, main search tolerance 6 ppm, FTMS 20 ppm and ITMS 0.5 Da. The design sheet's per-channel genotypes (E1-E3: light KO/heavy WT; E4-E6: light WT/heavy KO) match the SDRF exactly. Its MS-method column contradicts the raw headers and the Methods, so overriding it is correct.

file_mapping.evidence: PRIDE v3 files/all (projectAccessions == PXD038505) lists 66 .raw files. This SDRF holds 30 unique files (the A17-A26 RW8/RW9/RW10 files) and the sibling QC SDRF holds 36. The two sets do not overlap, and together they cover all 66 deposited raw files with none extra. Every file has exactly one light row and one heavy row, and all files are vendor .raw. These are exactly the 30 files in mqpar.xml, apart from the timestamp suffixes MaxQuant appended.

design_consistency.evidence: There are 20 sources: Control 1-4 plus KO 1-3 and WT 1-3, each split into a K4R6 dish and a K8R10 dish. The incorporation runs measure each dish separately, so treating each dish as its own source is supported. The key (source, biological replicate, technical replicate, fraction) is unique, and so is the key (source, assay, label). Characteristics are constant within each source. factor value[genotype] equals characteristics[genotype].

omission_safety.evidence: Nothing is asserted beyond the evidence. Control 1-4 appear only in the design sheet, as same-sample-in-both-channels mixes, with no stated biology, so their characteristics are 'not available'. Organism is the one inference for these rows, supported by the mouse-only search and the project organism. Donor stage, sex and strain each come from a verbatim Methods statement. The manifest discloses the MSA encoding, the use of 'SILAC light' for K4R6, and the omitted reduction/alkylation reagents.

deterministic_validation.evidence: I ran parse_sdrf validate-sdrf (sdrf_pipelines 0.1.7) myself under flock with bare template names. A union run with -t ms-proteomics -t vertebrates -t clinical-metadata exited 0 with one warning: 'C57BL/6 is not found in ncbitaxon'. Separate runs for each template also exited 0. sdrf-tools check exited 0 with status CLEAN, and sdrf-tools score gave 100/100.

findings.location: characteristics[strain or breed], rows of Cdkl5 sources
findings.message: parse_sdrf warns that 'C57BL/6' is not found in NCBITaxon.
findings.evidence: The vertebrates 1.1.0 template uses C57BL/6 as its own example, and EFO:0022397 'C57BL/6' exists. The warning is a limitation of the validator's ontology list, not an error in the value.

findings.message: Technical replicates 1, 2 and 3 are repeated injections that each used a different fragmentation method (CID, MSA, HCD), so they are not equivalent replicates.
findings.evidence: The raw headers show the method differs per index. Downstream tools that merge technical replicates will combine data from different methods, as the authors' MaxQuant search also did. Optionally, note this in the dataset README.

findings.message: The campaign asked for neurodegenerative diseases. CDKL5 deficiency disorder is a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, not a classic neurodegenerative disease.
findings.evidence: The paper calls CDD a DEE. Whether it is in scope is the campaign owner's decision; this does not affect the correctness of the SDRF.
